## Validation

Use feasibility checks, independent recomputation of objective terms, solver optimality gaps, and perturbation tests. Hold out no data because none are supplied; empirical validation is pending data acquisition. Compare optimization recommendations with network-simulation outcomes and verify that every recommendation satisfies capacity and policy constraints.

## Sensitivity and Robustness

Vary budget/capacity parameters, intervention effects, interaction strengths, and objective trade-off tolerances over statement-justified ranges. Report rank stability, Pareto hypervolume, worst-case objective values, and regret relative to the scenario-optimal portfolio. Weight sensitivity should be replaced by \(\epsilon\)-constraint and stakeholder-weight elicitation where possible.

## Falsification

Reject the model if: (i) the status quo dominates every proposed portfolio; (ii) small parameter perturbations cause unstable recommendations; (iii) selected interventions routinely violate capacities; (iv) network interactions add no explanatory or predictive value; or (v) recommendations depend on undocumented weights or fabricated data.

## Reviewer Risks

Main risks are arbitrary weights, ignored capacity constraints, unsupported causal effects, incomplete treatment of communities outside the boundary, network edges without evidence, and claims presented as results before execution. The truncated excerpt also makes complete requirement coverage unverifiable.

## Reproducibility Manifest

Record case ID, both hashes, source-summary path, full-statement version, variable/constraint dictionary, scenario definitions, solver and dependency versions, random seed (if simulation is stochastic), tolerances, and a single command that rebuilds all tables and figures.
